title: When the Well Sings
premise: Felix Fairweather hosts a small-town overnight radio show, and one October the call-in lines start filling with voices of people who died the week before—each asking Felix to pass messages to a family Felix never knew they had. Following the calls to their grandmother's abandoned house on Hollow Creek Road, Felix discovers they are the last heir of the town's founders, bound to a ritual that keeps something beneath the well fed and quiet. As frost creeps inward in patterns too deliberate to be weather, and the photographs keep adding chairs for relatives who never existed, Felix must decide whether to finish the founders' ritual—which requires a willing Fairweather to stay forever—or break it and let the thing below rise. With the found family of listeners who answered the final broadcast, Felix breaks the circle at the winter solstice, sealing the well not with a sacrifice but with every voice in town singing over it, though Felix's own reflection is left permanently out of sync.
about_author: Jonah Ashgrove is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent seven years taking calls from insomniacs, conspiracists, and the recently bereaved across three time zones. They write horror about small towns, dead frequencies, and the families we assemble from static.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During a routine overnight broadcast, a caller identifies herself as Maribel Doyle—who died six days ago—and asks Felix to tell her son the stove was never fixed. Felix assumes a prank, but the grief in the caller's voice is precise, specific, unbearable. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Second Call
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. More dead callers phone in over three nights, each with mundane messages and each knowing details of Felix's own childhood no stranger could. Station manager Priya Chandra notices Felix's declining composure and covers shifts without asking why. Emotional beat: denial cracking under accumulation.

chapters.title: Grandmother's House
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following an address one caller repeats like a lullaby, Felix reaches the derelict Fairweather house on Hollow Creek Road and finds it preserved mid-meal, as if the family simply stood up. A well behind the house hums when Felix speaks aloud. Emotional beat: dread mixed with inexplicable homesickness.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Every photograph in the house now includes an additional empty chair—kitchen scenes, weddings, funerals—positioned always facing the camera. When Felix takes one photo home, the chair appears in pictures there too, closer each hour. Emotional beat: the horror of being expected.

chapters.title: Listeners
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Felix, then stays anyway, and together they trace the callers: all died within a mile of the well across four generations. Priya, pragmatic and frightened, becomes Felix's first ally. Emotional beat: the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the town archive, Felix finds the founders' ledger: the Fairweathers made a bargain in 1891—a voice given freely to the well each generation, in exchange for the town's prosperity and mild winters. The final entry is unsigned. Emotional beat: inheritance as sentence.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Frost begins forming on windows across town in spiraling, identical patterns, always pointing toward Hollow Creek Road. The radio show's live callers now include living people begging Felix to make it stop. Emotional beat: private haunting going public.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Dead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On air, the dead callers sing in unison—an old hymn Felix somehow knows the harmony to without ever learning it. Listeners across town wake up humming it. Felix realizes the song is the ritual's first verse, and they've already started it. Emotional beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: Aunt Vesper
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A woman arrives claiming to be Felix's aunt—Vesper Fairweather, alive, ageless, and furious that Felix has been 'waking the house.' She explains the ritual's terms and offers to take Felix's place if Felix leaves town before solstice. Her kindness has teeth. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a relative's face.

chapters.title: Messages Delivered
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya helps Felix deliver the dead's final messages door to door; some recipients slam doors, one old man weeps with relief, and the town begins to remember what it agreed to forget. Grief becomes communal. Emotional beat: connection forged through obligation.

chapters.title: The Well Sings Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the well, Felix hears their own voice rising from below—recordings of broadcasts they never made, promises they never spoke, spoken in their cadence. The thing beneath is learning to be Felix. Emotional beat: identity under siege.

chapters.title: Vesper's Terms
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper reveals she was meant to be the 1991 sacrifice and fled, leaving her sister—Felix's grandmother—to go down instead. She wants Felix to finish it so her debt dies with them both. Emotional beat: cowardice dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Static Family
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya organizes the night-shift listeners—the insomniacs, the lonely, the bereaved—who've become Felix's true congregation. They agree to hold vigil at the house through the solstice. Emotional beat: found family choosing its shape.

chapters.title: The Photographs Finish
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the newest photos, the extra chair is occupied by a figure with Felix's face, and the other chairs fill with generations of Fairweathers, all waiting. The house's rooms begin rearranging themselves into a dining room set for many. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Left
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Behind the pantry, Felix finds grandmother Edith's hidden journal: she went willingly but left instructions for breaking the cycle—the ritual can be sealed not by one voice given, but by many voices given freely together, sung over the well until dawn. Emotional beat: hope hidden in a dead woman's hand.

chapters.title: Vesper Interferes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Vesper sabotages the vigil, cutting power and broadcasting Felix's voice from the well itself to lure listeners away. Priya holds the group together by doing what she does best: running the board, keeping everyone talking. Emotional beat: leadership born of fear.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The frost reaches the house's threshold, writing the ritual's final pattern across the floorboards. The dead callers speak with one voice, offering Felix a choice framed as kindness: finish alone and spare everyone, or risk everyone to spare yourself. Emotional beat: the corrupting logic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On solstice night, Felix opens every line and asks the town—not for silence, but for song. Living and dead voices braid together through the transmitter while the well rises to answer. Vesper, hearing her sister's voice among the dead, finally joins the hymn instead of fighting it. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into communion.

chapters.title: Beneath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, dreamlike. Pulled partway down the well, Felix meets the thing wearing their voice and sees it truly: not a monster but a hunger that learned loneliness first. Felix refuses it a single self to consume, offering instead the whole chorus above. Emotional beat: compassion as weapon.

chapters.title: Dawn Pattern
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. As sunrise breaks the solstice, the frost patterns complete and then dissolve. The well goes silent. The extra chair appears in one last photograph—empty, facing away. Vesper ages decades in a minute and finally looks mortal, and tired, and free. Emotional beat: exhaustion after survival.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Weeks later, Felix returns to the air with a new format: a show where anyone can leave a message for someone they lost, and sometimes, softly, an answer comes back. The dead callers don't return, but the line stays open. Emotional beat: grief made habitable.

chapters.title: Out of Sync
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, final. Mirrors still lag half a heartbeat behind Felix, and once a year, on the solstice, the whole town sings. In the last photograph of grandma's house, every chair is full, and Felix sits among them—almost. Emotional beat: belonging with a permanent scar.
